Nicknamed "'''the''' '''Maple Mamba'''",{{Cite web |title=Get to know the Maple Mamba, Duke's RJ Barrett {{!}} NCAA.com |url=https://www.ncaa.com/video/basketball-men/2019-03-06/mbk-duke-rj-barrett-maple-mamba |access-date=2026-05-02 |website=www.ncaa.com |language=en}} he was selected third overall in the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[New York Knicks]] after one year of [[college basketball]] with the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. Born in [[Toronto]] as the son of former basketball player [[Rowan Barrett]], Barrett shone at [[St. Marcellinus Secondary School]] in [[Mississauga]], [[Ontario]], before transferring to [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]]. He was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the consensus top recruit in the 2018 class, earning [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] and [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade National Player of the Year]] accolades in his final high school season whilst playing as a shooting guard a majority of the season. He was ranked the top player in his class by all recruiting services and was the first player since [[LeBron James]] to sweep all major awards in high school and win the national championship. With the [[Canada national under-19 basketball team|Canadian national under-19 team]], Barrett was named [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|MVP]] at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] after leading his team to a gold medal. He debuted for the senior team during [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup qualification (Americas)|qualification]] for the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup|2019 FIBA World Cup]]. ==Early life and career== Barrett was born in [[Toronto]], Ontario, to Kesha Duhaney and former professional basketball player [[Rowan Barrett]].{{cite web |title=RJ Barrett Bio |url=http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211767532&DB_OEM_ID=4200&Q_SEASON=2018 |publisher=Duke Athletics |access-date=January 4, 2018 |archive-date=June 27, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190627044257/http://www.goduke.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=211767532&DB_OEM_ID=4200&Q_SEASON=2018 |url-status=dead }} Early in his childhood, he developed an interest in basketball and played with a mini-hoop in his playroom in France, where his father was playing professional basketball at the time.{{cite web |last1=Grange |first1=Michael |title=Poster Boy: Rowan Barrett Jr. Rising |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/poster-boy-rowan-barrett-jr-rising/ |publisher=[[Sportsnet]] |access-date=January 5, 2019 |date=August 17, 2015}} In the 2005–06 season, he started playing organized basketball in the youth set-up of [[JDA Dijon Basket]].{{Cite web |date=August 24, 2023 |title=[Rétro] Quand R.J. Barrett, la star canadienne, jouait en mini-poussins en France |url=https://www.bebasket.fr/rj-barrett-france/ |access-date=August 26, 2023 |website=BeBasket |language=fr}} While living in France, Barrett attended a French school but was taught English by his mother.{{cite web |last1=Davis |first1=Seth |title=Canada rising: R.J. Barrett's college announcement will move him one step closer to conquering the world |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/149076/2017/11/08/canada-rising-r-j-barretts-college-announcement-will-move-him-one-step-closer-to-conquering-the-world/ |publisher=[[The Athletic]] |access-date=January 7, 2019 |date=November 8, 2017}} He lived in a number of countries due to his father's career. Barrett additionally played basketball with players his age through the clubs of which his father was a member.{{cite web |last1=Salvian |first1=Haley |title=Like father, like son: R.J. and Rowan Barrett |url=https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/rj-rowan-barrett-father-son-dynamic-1.4649826 |publisher=[[Canadian Broadcasting Corporation]] |access-date=January 6, 2019 |date=May 6, 2018}} His family settled in [[Mississauga]], Ontario in 2008, when his father left professional basketball. While growing up, he was also involved in [[association football|football]], [[100 metres]] sprinting, and the [[high jump]].{{cite news |last1=Ewing |first1=Lori |title=Canadian basketball star R.J. Barrett to jump a year ahead to join Class of 2018 |url=https://www.theglobeandmail.com/sports/basketball/canadian-basketball-star-rj-barrett-to-jump-a-year-ahead-to-join-class-of-2018/article35843179/ |website=[[The Globe and Mail]] |access-date=January 5, 2019 |date=July 31, 2017}} At age 12, after struggling in a basketball game and coming home crying, Barrett began focusing on basketball instead of football to avoid missing tournaments. At that age, he told his father that he wanted to be an [[List of NBA All-Stars|NBA All-Star]] and make the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame|Basketball Hall of Fame]]. He sometimes trained with [[Steve Nash]], his [[godparent|godfather]] and father's friend.{{cite web |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=RJ Barrett inherited a Canada that Vince Carter built |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/25707107/how-vince-carter-paved-way-rj-barrett |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 9, 2019 |date=January 8, 2019}} Barrett, under the guidance of his father, emerged as one of the best under-12 players in Ontario. He attended Horizon Jeunesse in Park Royal, Mississauga, leading his school team to a city title for Mississauga French elementary schools, where he was named [[most valuable player]] (MVP) despite facing older opponents. Barrett also played for the Regional Elite Development Academy (REDA) under-12 program on the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) circuit, facing many teams from the United States.{{cite web |last1=Colpitts |first1=Iain |title=Like father, like son |url=https://www.mississauga.com/community-story/3119703-like-father-like-son/ |website=[[The Mississauga News]] |access-date=January 5, 2019 |date=August 29, 2011}} When he was 12, he was identified by the Ontario Basketball Association as one of the best players in his age group, and he consequently trained with the [[Canada Basketball]] junior academy, through which he competed for the Ontario provincial team. By age 15, Barrett was generally playing the [[point guard]] position. On August 3, 2014, he scored 37 points and grabbed seven rebounds in a 93–53 win over Quebec at an under-15 provincial tournament.{{cite web |last1=Sbiet |first1=Tariq |title=Team Ontario 15s Prove Dominance, Rowan Barrett Jr Explodes for 37 |url=http://northpolehoops.com/2014/08/03/team-ontario-15s-prove-dominance-rowan-barrett-jr-explodes-for-37/ |publisher=North Pole Hoops |access-date=January 5, 2019 |date=August 3, 2014}} Through grades seven and eight, Barrett attended École Secondaire Jeunes Sans Frontières, a French language school in [[Brampton]].{{cite web |last1=Vallière |first1=Kim |title=R.J. Barrett, possible premier choix de la NBa et francophone |url=http://www.sympatico.ca/actualites/nouvelles/regions/ottawa-gatineau/r-j-barrett-possible-premier-choix-de-la-nba-et-francophone-1.3978124 |access-date=January 6, 2019 |language=fr |date=July 2, 2018}} ==High school career== ===St. Marcellinus (2014–2015)=== {{quote box |quote="While we don't often give praise in the early stages of a player's career (ninth grade), Rowan Barrett Jr (2019 6'4 wing) is proving to be the exception—a cold blooded killer, still out for blood. Barrett shakes the world in Canada's historic win over USA|date=July 8, 2017|website=Northpolehoops.com|access-date=July 9, 2017}} He subsequently led Canada to the title, tallying game-highs of 18 points and 12 rebounds in the championship game against Italy, and was named to [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup All-Tournament Team|the tournament's All-Star Five]] and also [[FIBA Under-19 World Cup MVP|the tournament Most Valuable Player]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/canada-routs-italy-capture-gold-fiba-u19-basketball-world-cup/|title=Canada routs Italy to capture gold at FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup |work=Sportsnet.ca|access-date=July 9, 2017}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/world/u19/2017/news/barrett-named-mvp-after-winning-canada-s-first-u19-title|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170713003239/http://www.fiba.com/world/u19/2017/news/barrett-named-mvp-after-winning-canada-s-first-u19-title|url-status=live|archive-date=July 13, 2017|title=Barrett named MVP after winning Canada's first U19 title|website=FIBA.basketball|date=July 9, 2017 |access-date=July 10, 2017}} Averaging 21.6 points a game, he was also the leading scorer of the tournament.{{Cite web|url=https://fiba.com/world/u19/2017/playerstats|title=Players statistics of the FIBA U19 Basketball World Cup 2017 – FIBA.basketball|website=FIBA.basketball|access-date=July 12, 2017}} In June 2018, he made his debut on Canada's senior men's national team, scoring 16 points in a 97–62 win over China.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/olympics/summer/rj-barrett-canada-basketball-victory-national-team-debut-1.4719457|title=R.J. Barrett leads Canada to victory in national team debut {{!}} CBC Sports|date=June 23, 2018|first=Jim|last=Morris|agency=The Canadian Press|publisher=Canadian Broadcasting Corporation|access-date=December 8, 2018}} On May 24, 2022, Barrett agreed to a three-year commitment to play with the Canadian senior men's national team.{{Cite web |title=FOURTEEN ATHLETES COMMITTED TO REPRESENT CANADA AS SENIOR MEN'S NATIONAL TEAM SUMMER CORE REVEALED |url=https://www.basketball.ca/news/athletes-committed-to-represent-canada-as-senior-mens-national-team-summer-core-revealed |access-date=May 24, 2022 |website=Canada Basketball}} On September 3, they qualified to the quarter-finals of [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]], in the process securing a berth at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics - Men's tournament|2024 Summer Olympics]]."{{cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10088193-shai-gilgeous-alexander-on-canada-qualifying-for-olympics-were-a-part-of-history|title=Shai Gilgeous-Alexander on Canada Qualifying for Olympics: 'We're a Part of History'|last=Rapp|first=Timothy|website=[[The Bleacher Report]]|date=September 3, 2023|access-date=September 10, 2023}} Barrett ultimately sealed the victory with a 3 point shot and won the bronze medal over the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States]] in the third-place game. Barrett outplayed his [[New York Knicks|Knicks]] teammates [[Jalen Brunson]] and [[Josh Hart]] with 23 points on 50% shooting from the field.{{cite news|url=https://heavy.com/sports/new-york-knicks/rj-barrett-beats-brunson-hart/|title=Clutch RJ Barrett Helps Canada Beat Team USA for Historic Bronze Finish|last=Almo|first=Alder|website=[[Heavy (website)|Heavy]]|access-date=September 10, 2023 |date=September 10, 2023}} He combined with [[Dillon Brooks]] (39 points) and [[Shai Gilgeous-Alexander]] (31 points) for 93 points.
